slots.title: Cutting and raising at the same time
slots.hook: Banks are cutting rates two weeks before the RBA might raise them.
slots.angle: Dozens of lenders cut variable rates for new customers over the past month (ABC, 14 Sep) while markets price roughly an 80% chance of a rise on 29 Sep. Banks are fighting over a shrinking pool of borrowers, so the discount goes to whoever asks. Existing customers get nothing unless they ask.
slots.filmWindow: Films today in the batch. Numbers hold until 29 Sep.
slots.cta: Save this for the day after the 29th.
slots.onScreen: Cutting for new customers. Raising for everyone.
slots.notes: System built Wednesday evening, no batch filmed 16 Sep. Angle rolls into the reprice window reel W3-01 and the RBA react W2-08.

script.spoken:
Banks are cutting rates two weeks before the RBA might raise them.

Read that again.

Dozens of lenders have cut variable rates in the past month. For new customers.

At the same time, markets are pricing about an 80 per cent chance the Reserve Bank lifts the cash rate on the 29th.

Both can be true. Banks are fighting over a shrinking pool of borrowers, so the discount goes to whoever walks in the door.

If you've been with your bank more than a year and haven't asked, you're funding that discount.

Ask before the 29th. It's a phone call.

slots.hook: Seven lenders cut investor borrowing power by up to 20%. Nobody sent you a letter.
slots.angle: Since the Budget quarantined rental losses on established property bought after 12 May 2026 (from 1 July 2027), lenders have started removing the negative gearing add-back from how they assess investors. Same income, same rent, less borrowing. Describe the mechanism, do not name the lenders.
slots.filmWindow: Build on batch day. Policy is set, numbers are stable.
slots.cta: Send this to anyone bidding on an investment property this spring.

script.setup: Carousel, build from the copy. Navy, sky headings, white body, 1080x1350. Do not name the lenders.
slides: Cover
Seven lenders cut investor borrowing power by up to 20%. Nobody sent you a letter.
What changed
In the May Budget the government said rental losses on established property bought after 12 May 2026 stop offsetting your wages from 1 July 2027. New builds are exempt.
Why your bank cares
For years lenders added the tax benefit of a rental loss back into your income when they assessed you. If the concession is going, so is the add-back.
Three columns
Before: tax saving added back to income · Now: assessed on the cash shortfall alone · Result: up to 20% less borrowing on some calculators
Who feels it
The nine in ten investors with one or two properties, buying the next one this spring. Same job, same rent, smaller number.
The trade-off
The new number is more honest. It's what the property actually costs you each month. Not a bad thing to know before you bid.
Close
Get your capacity re-run before you bid. / Not after. A pre-approval from May might not be a pre-approval today.

slots.title: The bank's favourite structure
slots.hook: The bank's favourite loan structure is the one that costs you the most.
slots.angle: Deal breakdown, de-identified composite. A client came in with a home and an investment property on one facility with one bank. Cross-collateralisation ties every property to every loan. Sell one and the bank revalues the lot and can hold the proceeds. We split them: ring-fenced loans keep each property's equity yours. Trade-off: more paperwork, sometimes two sets of fees, and it takes a broker who will do the work.
slots.filmWindow: Not filmed 16 Sep. Film in one 45-minute sitting Thu 17 or Fri 18 morning, or roll into the Wed 23 Sep batch and post in week 2.
slots.cta: Save this before your next purchase.
slots.onScreen: One loan, two houses. Guess who benefits.

script.setup: Desk plus a second angle 30 to 40 degrees off, Lane B. Outfit 2. Clap at the top of each take, cut to B on every point.
script.spoken:
The bank's favourite loan structure is the one that costs you the most.

It's called cross-collateralisation, and most people who have it don't know they have it.

Here's how it happens. You own your home. You buy an investment property. The bank offers to lend against both together. One facility, one application, less paperwork. Sounds helpful.

Now here's what you actually signed.

Every property secures every loan. The bank has a claim over the lot.

Sell one, and the bank revalues everything before it lets go. If values have dipped, it can hold your sale proceeds to fix up the loan on the one you kept.

Want to refinance one property to a better lender? You can't. They come as a set.

And every valuation, every top-up, runs through one credit team's view of your whole position.

The alternative is ring-fencing. Each property, its own loan. Use equity from one as a cash deposit on the next, but keep the securities separate.

The trade-off is real. More paperwork, sometimes two sets of fees, and it takes a broker willing to do the work instead of ticking the bank's box.

But you keep your options. And over ten years, options are worth more than convenience.
script.onScreen: One loan, two houses. Guess who benefits. Then each point as text as you say it.
script.numbers: None. The four points appear as text on each turn.

script.caption:
The bank's favourite loan structure is the one that costs you the most.

Cross-collateralisation. One facility over your home and your investment. Less paperwork, and here's what you signed:

→ every property secures every loan
→ sell one and the bank revalues the lot first, and can hold your proceeds
→ refinance one to a better lender? They come as a set
→ every valuation runs through one credit team's view of everything

The alternative is ring-fencing. Each property, its own loan. Equity from one becomes a cash deposit on the next.

The trade-off: more paperwork, sometimes two sets of fees, and a broker willing to do the work.

Over ten years, options beat convenience. Save this before your next purchase.

slots.hook: Nine in ten property investors own one or two places. The greedy landlord is mostly fiction.
slots.angle: ATO data: about 71% of investors hold one property, another 19% hold two. Investor loan numbers fell 8.6% in the June quarter and annual growth collapsed from 19.4% to 2.8%. Most of these people are building a retirement the government has shown it cannot fund. Trade-off: some investors do hoard, and a concession is not a plan.

Nine in ten property investors own one or two places. The greedy landlord is mostly fiction.
The ATO's own numbers (three columns)
71% own one property · 19% own two · About 1% own six or more
Who they are
Nurses, tradies, teachers, small business owners. Mostly on ordinary incomes, mostly building a retirement they don't trust the government to fund.
What's happening now
Investor loan numbers fell 8.6% in the June quarter. Annual growth went from 19.4% to 2.8%. The investors are leaving, not hoarding.
The trade-off
Some investors do hoard. Some suburbs have been priced by investors. And negative gearing is a concession, not a plan.
The real problem
1.2 million homes promised. Delivery is now 18 months late. You can't tax your way to a house that hasn't been built.
Close

slots.title: Insurance from the person who sets the price
slots.hook: Fixing your rate is buying insurance from the person who sets the price.
slots.angle: The only one who wins on fixed over a full cycle is the bank. Right now the best fixed rates sit above the best variable, so fixing is a hedge against a rise, not a discount. Name who it is right for: the borrower who genuinely cannot hold a rise. Certainty has a price and that is fine if you know you are paying it.
slots.filmWindow: Not filmed 16 Sep. Film in one 45-minute sitting Thu 17 or Fri 18 morning, or roll into the Wed 23 Sep batch and post in week 2.

script.spoken:
Fixing your rate is buying insurance from the person who sets the price.

Over a full cycle, variable has beaten fixed almost every time. The bank prices the fixed rate, and the bank is not in the business of losing that bet.

Right now the best fixed rates sit above the best variable ones. So fixing today isn't a discount. It's a hedge.

And a hedge is fine, if you know that's what you're buying.

Who it's right for: the borrower who genuinely couldn't hold another rise.

Certainty has a price. Just know you're paying it.

slots.title: Does my HECS debt matter?
slots.hook: Your HECS debt is costing you more borrowing power than your car loan.
slots.angle: Client question this week. Lenders treat the compulsory repayment as a fixed monthly outgoing, scaled to your income band, so a five-figure balance can knock six figures off capacity. New this year: some lenders can ignore a HELP debt that will be cleared within about a year. Trade-off: paying it out of your deposit can leave you short on deposit. It is a trade, not a rule.
slots.filmWindow: Not filmed 16 Sep. Film in one 45-minute sitting Thu 17 or Fri 18 morning, or roll into the Wed 23 Sep batch and post in week 2.
slots.cta: Comment HECS and I'll do the long version.

script.setup: Desk, phone, Lane A. Outfit 2 (shirt change). The car works too, parked, engine off.
script.spoken:
Your HECS debt is costing you more borrowing power than your car loan.

A client asked this week whether a forty thousand dollar balance mattered. It matters more than the number suggests.

Lenders don't look at what you owe. They look at the repayment coming out of your pay, and they treat it like a loan you can't cancel.

On a typical calculator, that's six figures off what you can borrow.

Two things changed this year. Some lenders can now ignore a balance you'll clear within about a year. And paying it out of your deposit can leave you short on deposit.

It's a trade, not a rule.

slots.title: The number on your file that kills the deal
slots.hook: There's a number on your file that can kill the deal before the rate matters.
slots.angle: APRA's debt-to-income cap has been live since February: lenders can write no more than 20% of new loans at six times income or more. Total debt includes the new loan, cards, car, HECS. Household income $150k means roughly $900k of total debt before you are in the capped bucket. Who it hits first: investors on their second and third loan. Trade-off: it is a cap on the lender's book, not a hard no to you, and a good broker knows which lenders have room.
slots.cta: Save this. You'll want it before your next purchase.

slots.title: RBA decision react
slots.hook: VARIANT A (rise): They raised. Here's the one thing that changes for you today. VARIANT B (hold): They held. Don't read that as the top.
slots.angle: Live react, filmed 2:45 to 3:00pm after the 2:30pm decision. Both scripts pre-written in the shot list. Angle for either outcome: what it changes for someone with a settlement in the next 90 days. Your capacity is tested at the rate plus a 3% buffer, so a quarter-point move shifts borrowing power by roughly 2 to 3% (illustrative). Never a rate, never a product.
slots.filmWindow: Tue 29 Sep, 2:45 to 3:00pm. Phone at the desk. Post by 3:15pm.
